The debate hinges on whether Figma's strong revenue growth and positive free cash flow offset unresolved regulatory risk and structural profitability challenges.

The bull emphasizes [C:fig-ocf-proves-core-generation] and [C:fig-gaap-sbc-non-cash-distinction] to argue that GAAP losses are accounting artifacts masking a viable cash-generative business, while the bear contends that [C:fig-ocf-contradicts-operating-loss] exposes a fundamental gap: a company reporting $250.7M operating cash flow against $275M operating losses (excluding IPO charge) cannot sustain growth without either resolving the contradiction or accepting ongoing losses as structural.

On the OFAC matter, both sides agree disclosure has occurred, but disagree on materiality: the bull treats [C:fig-ofac-disclosed-not-determined] as a managed contingency, while the bear flags [C:fig-ofac-unquantifiable-tail-exposure] as tail risk equity holders bear fully if violations are determined.

The central evidentiary contest is whether [C:fig-sbc-dilution-offset-by-growth] (bull: 41% revenue growth exceeds dilution risk) or [C:fig-sbc-dilution-permanent-compounding] (bear: 129% SBC/revenue ratio is unsustainable even at 41% growth).

Figma faces two material risk factors: [RF2C69] an unresolved OFAC enforcement matter stemming from voluntary self-disclosure of potential sanctions violations, with no accrued loss and potential for substantial fines; and [RFEA09] persistent operating losses of approximately $275M in FY2025 (excluding one-time IPO charge) despite 41% revenue growth.
These are offset by [RF6C51] strong net dollar retention of 136% and [RF6687] organic revenue growth of 41% YoY, driven by proven land-and-expand dynamics ($100k+ ARR cohort grew 46% YoY).
Positive free cash flow of $242.7M in FY2025 and zero debt provide financial flexibility, but [RF3AA0] elevated stock-based compensation at 129% of revenue masks persistent dilution risk.
[RF6C51] Net dollar retention decline below 130%: deterioration in this metric would signal weakening land-and-expand dynamics and validate bear thesis on customer durability.

[RF3AA0] Post-IPO share repurchase activity: initiation of material buyback program would offset SBC dilution and signal management confidence in valuation; absence of buybacks despite $405.7M cash would validate dilution risk.
